chunks: ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the missing person: what should his wife do? He said:

So long as she remains silent about him and is patient, she is to be left as she is. But if she brings her case to the authority, he gives her a term of four years, then writes to the region in which he went missing and inquiry is made about him. If news comes that he is alive, she remains patient. If no news comes of his being alive until the four years pass, the guardian of the missing husband is summoned and asked: does the missing man have wealth? If he has wealth, maintenance is spent on her from it until his life or death becomes known. If he has no wealth, the guardian is told: spend on her. If he does so, then she has no way to remarry so long as he spends on her. But if he refuses to spend on her, the authority compels him to issue one divorce at the beginning of the waiting period while she is in a state of purity. Then the divorce of the guardian becomes the divorce of the husband. If her husband comes before her waiting period ends from the day the guardian divorced her, and he then decides to take her back, then she is his wife, and she remains with him with two divorces left. But if the waiting period ends before he comes and takes her back, then she becomes lawful for husbands, and the first has no claim over her.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ سِنِينَ: the four-year period of waiting and inquiry
key_terms.الْعِدَّةِ: the legally prescribed waiting period after divorce
key_terms.الْمَفْقُودِ: a missing person whose life or death is unknown
key_terms.الْوَالِي: the governing authority who oversees and enforces the legal procedure
key_terms.طَلَاقُ الْوَلِيِّ: the divorce effected by the guardian under authority
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth from which the wife may be maintained
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الزَّوْجِ: the guardian or family representative of the missing husband

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the wife of a missing husband in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling regarding the wife of a missing husband and the role of the authority and guardian in handling her case. It outlines the four-year waiting period, investigation, financial maintenance, and the circumstances under which divorce and remarriage become permissible.
